original.title: The Agenda-Setting Function of Mass Media

core_idea: The media may not tell people what to think, but they are stunningly successful in telling them what to think about. Issues that get more coverage become more salient on the public agenda. Second-level agenda-setting adds that media also shape which attributes of an issue stand out.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Which issues do media cover, and does that match what the public sees as important?
How do media shape the salience of attributes of candidates or issues?
Typical data: content analysis matched with surveys, time-series.
common_mistakes: Confusing agenda-setting (what to think about) with framing (how to think about it).
Comparing media and public agendas without a time order.
Ignoring social media and intermedia agenda-setting.
